description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Trivy native fixture that carries records from which no message can be obtained by any consulted route. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/trivy.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. The key names are those of the negative template expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json, and every key the tool's positive expected file expected/trivy.rows.json uses is reused here with the same meaning, so one generic loader reads all of them.
scanner_class: per record -- vuln, secret or misconfig -- taken from the section array the record was read from. Trivy is the one tool in AAP 0.5.4's class table whose scanner_class is not fixed, and that variation survives a rejection: the two rejected records are attributed to their sections before the message step rejects them, which is why each rejection below names its section.
scanner_class_derivation: trivy.SUPPORTED_SECTIONS, the single seam through which a class is established, read through trivy.scanner_class_for_section. The class is bound at the moment the traversal chooses an array and never from record content. There is deliberately no module-level SCANNER_CLASS constant in this adapter, unlike every sibling.
scanner_class_falsifiability: Row 2 is the record that fails if the derivation is ever inverted: it is a secret whose only text is the rule Title "Asymmetric Private Key", and a content sniff looking for a matched value would find none and could plausibly class it as a misconfiguration. Its class is secret because /Results/2/Secrets is the array it was read from, and for no other reason. The same test applies to the rejections: rejection 0 sits in Misconfigurations and rejection 1 in Vulnerabilities, and a rejection that lost its section would lose the only evidence of which adapter branch classified it.

fixture.derivation: Two records of the positive fixture with their message routes defeated, one record of this run's own raw artifact with its first route defeated, and nothing else changed anywhere. /Results/0/Misconfigurations/0 is the positive fixture's own DS-0031 record with its Title and Description members removed, leaving only the Message member the adapter does not consult for a misconfiguration. The axios vulnerability's Title and Description are emptied to "" rather than removed, so the two variants of one class -- key absent, and key present but empty -- are both covered. /Results/1 and its DS-0026 record are the second Dockerfile Target, carrying the near miss: that record is harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json's own DS-0026 record on the same file with its Title removed and every other member left byte-identical, so its Description carries text and it becomes a row. Every other member of every record here is its source's, unedited. Throughout this file, "the positive fixture" and "the positive sibling" name the declared-derived document this fixture is derived from -- oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-trivy-features.json and its expected file oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/derived-trivy-features.rows.json, whose nine finding records and nine rows are the ones cited by index below. Neither term names oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/trivy.json, which is a byte-for-byte copy of harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json carrying only its three DS-0026 misconfiguration records, nor that file's expected file expected/trivy.rows.json.
fixture.shape_fidelity: A Trivy 0.74.0 filesystem report. Every member the adapter reads appears in report.go's own spelling: Results[] with Target, Class and Type; the three finding arrays; Packages with Identifier.PURL; MisconfSummary; CauseMetadata.StartLine; PkgIdentifier.PURL; PkgPath; CweIDs; and a CVSS table keyed by source. An emptied Title is a shape a producer really can emit -- the field is a plain string in the struct, not an optional -- so the emptied pair is a defeated route rather than an invented shape.
fixture.provenance: Derived rather than captured whole, and stated as such rather than papered over. harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json holds three records, all DS-0026 "No HEALTHCHECK defined" misconfigurations over three Dockerfiles, with zero vulnerabilities and zero secrets, because the twelve authoritative globs contain no dependency manifest for the vulnerability scanner to resolve and no matched secret for the secret scanner to report. Exactly one record below descends from that artifact -- row 1's, which is its R-bindings DS-0026 record with the Title removed -- and the other four descend from the positive fixture. No record below is byte-identical to any record in harness/artifacts/raw/ or under harness/artifacts/logs/, and no record in those trees is message-less, which is the whole reason this fixture has to be derived: AAP 0.6.2 requires a negative fixture per rejection condition whether or not this run's own artifacts contain the case.
fixture.fixture_is_never_edited_to_suit_these_ro: These rows are re-derived when the fixture changes, which is what the recorded sha256 above makes visible. The fixture is the input and this file is the assertion; the dependency runs one way. That rule decided the one place where this file and its own brief disagree -- see discrepancies_recorded, entry 1 -- in favour of the fixture.
fixture.carries_no_secret_material: The string "Match" does not occur in the fixture at all, and the only occurrence of "Secret" is the section key "Secrets" at line 105. The single secret record carries RuleID, Category, Severity, Title, StartLine and EndLine and no matched value, no Code excerpt and no redaction. So the guarantee that no secret value reaches a field is structural here rather than dependent on a redaction being correct, and the grep in how_to_check_this_file has nothing it could find.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- the artifact carries no version "2.1.0" and no runs array, which are the two members that together make an artifact SARIF, so it cannot route to the shared SARIF adapter
routing.trivy_native_markers: SchemaVersion 2, a Trivy object carrying Version, and a Results array -- read as the native Trivy shape and keyed to the runner that wrote it
routing.routing_decision: native trivy -> normalize.adapters.trivy.adapt, keyed by the runner that wrote the artifact rather than by sniffing the document
routing.not_a_shape_failure: The artifact routes cleanly and is parsed in full. Its defect is two records, not its shape, so parse status is partial rather than failed and the run continues. An artifact matching neither SARIF nor a known native shape is the halt case, and it is not this one: that is fixtures/unknown-shape.json. A halt is likewise not reachable through the unsupported-section route here -- see counts.unsupported_finding_sections.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative test asserts the direction that actually goes wrong: this native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter. A permissive detector accepting it as SARIF would find no runs array, return an empty result set, and an empty result set is indistinguishable from a clean scan. That test is test_shape_routing_negative.py; this file asserts the rows and the rejections, not the detector.

message_routes.three_routes_is_the_secret_case: A secret has three routes, which is the maximum any section has: the already-redacted Match first, exactly as AAP 0.5.4 states, with Title and Description behind it so that a secret carrying no Match still carries the words the tool did write instead of being rejected. A vulnerability and a misconfiguration have two each.
message_routes.the_multi_route_problem: A record is only message-less once every route its section has is defeated. Defeating Title alone leaves Description to succeed and produces a row rather than a rejection, and this fixture holds that near miss on purpose: /Results/1/Misconfigurations/0 has no Title, its Description carries text, and it is row 1. So the two rejected records each have both of their section's routes defeated, and the fixture demonstrates the boundary rather than asserting it in prose.
message_routes.message_is_not_a_route_for_a_misconfigur: Trivy gives a misconfiguration a third text member, Message, and the adapter deliberately does not consult it: it is the remediation instruction rather than the finding's message, and AAP 0.5.4 names Title and Description as the sources. Rejection 0 is the record that holds that decision to account -- it carries a Message with real text and is still rejected, so a future edit that quietly adds Message to the misconfiguration route tuple turns this expected file red instead of passing unnoticed.
message_routes.no_message_is_synthesised: No message is ever manufactured from another field. Not from the rule identifier, not from the package name, not from the path, and not from the remediation Message. A rejected record contributes no row at all, so there is nothing to fill; and the assertion is checkable rather than declarative -- see how_to_check_this_file, which compares every surviving row's message against each rejected record's rule identifier, package name and path as substrings in both directions.
message_routes.empty_is_absent: _message treats a present-but-empty or whitespace-only string as no message, through _non_empty_string. That is why rejection 1's Title of "" and Description of "" defeat both routes rather than producing a row whose message is the empty string -- message is one of emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS and an empty required field would make the CSV round trip lossy, since an empty cell means null.
message_routes.a_non_string_route_is_a_different_class: A consulted field present as a number, an object or an array is malformed_record rather than missing_message, named with the field and the observed type. Neither defective record here takes that branch: every consulted member is a string or absent. That branch's fixture is reject-trivy-malformed-record.json.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.root_independence: Every Target in this fixture is already root-relative and the recorded path base for trivy is the scan root itself, so joining onto the base and relativizing back to the root returns the reported string unchanged. The one per-record refinement is likewise root-relative. These rows therefore hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the trivy entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.why_the_merged_artifact_is_root_relative: The runner invokes trivy fs once per scope directory, because that subcommand takes exactly one path, and its merge step prefixes every part's Target with that part's own ArtifactName and sets the merged ArtifactName to ".". The recorded metadata states that, which is why the base is the scan root rather than any one directory.
resolution_context.path_base_caveat: That base holds for the merged artifact only. The same metadata records that the eighteen retained per-directory reports under logs/trivy.parts/ are not root-anchored and must be read with per_section_target semantics and an explicit section_base. This fixture is the merged shape, so section_base is null and passing one would be wrong rather than harmless.
resolution_context.target_is_the_base: path comes from the enclosing Results[].Target, refined by a per-record path where the section supplies one. Only Vulnerabilities declares such a field -- PkgPath -- so a secret and a misconfiguration take their Target unrefined. paths.resolve_trivy_path owns every base decision; the adapter relativizes, joins and strips nothing itself.
resolution_context.per_record_refinement_in_this_fixture: Exactly one, on row 4. Its Target is "Node.js", which names an ecosystem rather than a file, and its PkgPath names the manifest the package was found in -- core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json, five lines at the pin. The refinement is relative, is not the Target restated, and "Node.js" is not a container, so the resolved path is a tree_file and the row is in scope on the strength of the refinement rather than of the Target.
resolution_context.severity_source: Severity is passed as the label and the CVSS table as the scores, and severity.py decides between them: the native label governs wherever it is in the mapped vocabulary and a score is consulted only where no mapped label exists. Every surviving row here carries a mapped label, so severity_basis is label on all five and no score is ever consulted -- including on row 4, whose record does carry a CVSS table.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: The four-level precedence is shared: a package URL on the record, then a package URL on the matching enclosing Packages[] entry, then <ecosystem>:<name>@<version> from the record's own fields, then the same from the enclosing package's fields. Levels 1 and 2 are exercised here, on rows 4 and 3; levels 3 and 4 are not.
resolution_context.start_line: Section-dependent by the artifact's own shape. A secret states StartLine directly and a misconfiguration states it inside CauseMetadata, with the top level tried first; a vulnerability declares no line information at all. Absence is never a rejection -- only a start_line that is present and is not a usable line number is, and that condition's fixture is reject-trivy-non-integer-start-line.json.

rejection_boundary.statement: A record with no message is a rejection. A record with a message that is merely terse, uninformative, or drawn from a lower-preference route is a kept row. The two rejected records here have every route their section offers defeated; row 1 has its first route defeated and its second intact, and it is a row.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: message is one of emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS -- the seven fields that are never absent -- and emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS is exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate. A record with no message therefore has no valid row representation: emit.py raises on a null required field rather than writing one, and the CSV's empty cell means null, so an empty string would not survive the round trip either. Dropping the record would hide it and synthesising a message from a neighbouring field would invent tool output. Counting it under a named class is the only outcome that neither drops the record nor manufactures its content.

not_a_rejection.case: a record whose first message route is defeated but whose second carries text
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row whose message comes from the surviving route
not_a_rejection.evidence: /Results/1/Misconfigurations/0 has no Title and a Description with text, and is row 1. This is the near miss the fixture exists to hold: it is what a reader gets wrong when they defeat only Title.

not_a_rejection.case: a record whose only text is a member outside its section's route tuple
not_a_rejection.expected: a rejection, not a row -- the inverse of the case above
not_a_rejection.evidence: /Results/0/Misconfigurations/0 carries a Message with real text and no Title or Description, and is rejection 0. Message is not a misconfiguration route, so text being present in the document is not the same as a message being obtainable.

not_a_rejection.case: a path resolving outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: Row 3 resolves to dev/package-lock.json, which no glob covers, and is kept and marked. Out of scope means kept and marked, never rejected.

not_a_rejection.case: a Target that names no file in the tree
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row, resolved through the section's per-record refinement
not_a_rejection.evidence: Row 4's Target is "Node.js". The row exists because PkgPath refines it to a real file; the Target itself never becomes a path and contributes nothing to non_filesystem_paths.

not_a_rejection.case: a severity literal outside every mapped vocabulary
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row banded Info on the unmapped_literal basis and disclosed in severity-map.md
not_a_rejection.evidence: Not reached here. Row 3's UNKNOWN looks unmapped and is not: severity.py's label table bands NEGLIGIBLE, INFO, INFORMATIONAL, UNKNOWN and NONE to Info, so the basis is label and severity_basis_unmapped_literal stays 0.

rejection_boundary.no_guessed_message: Neither rejected record is given a message from its rule identifier, its package name, its path, its remediation Message, its Resolution, its References or its PrimaryURL. Each of those members is present on at least one of the two records, and none of them is a message route.
rejection_boundary.the_defective_records_are_otherwise_well: Deliberately, so each rejection is attributable to the message alone. Both are JSON objects; both sit in a supported section, so the class is established; both carry a valid rule identifier; and both have a Target that resolves and a severity that maps. Nothing but the message could have rejected either one.

counts.raw_count_unit: Results[] x one element of Vulnerabilities[], Secrets[] or Misconfigurations[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction, summing only the three supported sections
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("trivy", doc), whose traversal sums the lengths of the three supported section arrays across every Results[] element and builds no row, resolves no path, reads no message and maps no severity. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing. reconcile imports nothing from the adapter and the adapter imports nothing from reconcile, so the two readings cannot share a line of code.
counts.records_by_section_reconciles_too: records_vulnerabilities 3 + records_secrets 1 + records_misconfigurations 3 == 7 == raw_finding_records. Those three counters are bumped by each section array's length before its elements are walked, so they count the rejected records as well and are a decomposition of the same 7 rather than a second measurement of the rows.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.note: Named here rather than restated with their values. The counters block below is the single measurement, and a number carried twice inside one document is a number that can drift; counters_note gives the reason each of the four is zero, and one of them is zero for a reason worth reading.

unsupported_finding_sections.state_in_this_fixture: present and empty on every one of the five Results[] elements
unsupported_finding_sections.expectation: trivy.validate_finding_sections returns None. An unsupported finding section that is present and empty satisfies "validated empty" and does not halt.
unsupported_finding_sections.why_this_is_load_bearing_here: validate_finding_sections runs over every element before a single row is built, so a non-empty Licenses or ExperimentalModifiedFindings anywhere in this fixture would raise trivy.UnsupportedTrivySection and pre-empt both rejections -- the artifact would halt the run and this file would assert nothing. Keeping both sections empty is what makes the missing_message rejections reachable, and it is stated rather than left to the silence of not mentioning it.
unsupported_finding_sections.not_to_be_blurred_with: The non-empty twin is fixtures/halt-trivy-unsupported-section.json, whose expected file records the halt. Nothing in this file expects a halt, and nothing in that one expects a rejection.

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned as partial where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and both rejected records are counted under their class, with the reason each earned retained. This is deliberately not normalize.reconcile's STATUS_PASS / STATUS_FAIL / STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE vocabulary, which describes an assertion's outcome rather than an artifact's parse.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/trivy.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty-three authored keys, one records_* per supported section, one rows_class_* per scanner class, one path_kind_* per path kind and one severity_basis_* per severity basis, thirty-eight in total. Every key is listed above with its value, including the zeros, because a missing key is ambiguous between "zero" and "not measured".
counters_note: Three readings a reviewer must not "correct". First, the asymmetry between records_* and the row counters is the classification order made visible, not a miscount: records_vulnerabilities 3 and records_misconfigurations 3 count every record in those arrays, while rows_class_vuln 2 and rows_class_misconfig 2 count only the rows, and the difference is exactly the two rejected records. Second, multi_valued_cwe_records is 0 even though a record in this fixture carries two CWE identifiers. That record is rejection 1, and the counter is bumped after the message step, so its CweIDs are never collected and no ascending-numeric selection is ever made on them; the counter is a property of the rows, and a rejected record has none. multi_location_records, multi_valued_cve_records and non_filesystem_paths are 0 for reasons that need no such care -- every record names one location, cve is collected from VulnerabilityID alone which holds one identifier, and every resolved path names a file in the scanned tree. Third, severity_cvss_entries_present is 1 rather than 2: both the row 4 record and the rejection 1 record carry a CVSS table, and only the row's is counted, for the same reason. The counter records what was available to a row, not what the document contained.

corroboration.note: Four of the five surviving records are the positive fixture's records unedited -- DS-0029, the private-key secret, NSWG-ECO-519 and CVE-2017-16137 -- and the positive sibling hand-derived each of them independently, as its rows 1, 3, 5 and 8. All twelve fields of all four agree with the rows below, including the two values a reader is most likely to get wrong: NSWG-ECO-519's package_coordinate is the PURL pkg:npm/handlebars@4.5.3 from the matching enclosing Packages[] entry rather than the ecosystem coordinate npm:handlebars@4.5.3, and CVE-2017-16137's path is the PkgPath refinement rather than its Target. That is two independent hand-derivations of the same records reaching the same answer, which is a stronger check than either one alone. Row 1 is the only surviving row with no counterpart there, because its record is new to this fixture.
corroboration.not_corroborated_by_the_dataset: The run's own three trivy rows are DS-0026 misconfigurations over three Dockerfiles, and two of them name files this fixture also names -- but none of them is a row below. The dataset's DS-0026 rows carry the message "No HEALTHCHECK defined", which is their records' Title; row 1's message is its Description, precisely because the Title was removed to build the near miss. So findings.json confirms no row here, and the near-identity of the paths is recorded rather than left to look like agreement.

rows.message: You should add HEALTHCHECK instruction in your docker container images to perform the health check on running containers.
nodejs-debug: Regular expression Denial of Service

row_order: Results[] in document order, the three sections in trivy.SUPPORTED_SECTIONS order within each element -- Vulnerabilities, then Secrets, then Misconfigurations, whatever order the document's keys happen to be in -- and each section's elements in order. The two rejected records occupy positions in that traversal and simply produce no row, so the surviving rows keep their relative order and close up: raw record 1 becomes row 0 and raw record 5 becomes row 3. Each row's index below is its row_index under row_derivations.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Misconfigurations, which SUPPORTED_SECTIONS maps to misconfig
row_derivations.rule_id_source: /Results/0/Misconfigurations/1/ID -- the field _SECTION_RULE_ID_FIELD names for this section
row_derivations.message_note: Title is preferred over Description, and this record carries both. Its Message -- "'--no-install-recommends' flag is missed: 'apt-get update && apt install -y bash tini libc6 libpam-modules krb5-user libnss3 procps net-tools logrotate libssl-dev'" -- is the located instance and is not consulted, which is the same decision that rejects the sibling record at index 0 of this array.
row_derivations.start_line_note: A misconfiguration states its line inside CauseMetadata; _SECTION_START_LINE_PATHS tries the top-level StartLine first, finds none, then reads CauseMetadata.StartLine. 36 is within the file's real length, and the record's EndLine of 48 is not read -- the schema has one line field.
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: CweIDs is declared on DetectedVulnerability only, so a misconfiguration carries none by the artifact's shape
row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: cve is collected from VulnerabilityID, which this section's records do not carry
row_derivations.package_coordinate_absence_is_not_a_reje: Misconfigurations is outside _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS: this is a finding about a file, not about a package, so the field is legitimately absent and the record still becomes a row.
row_derivations.in_scope_note: The glob's mid-path ** matches the docker/ segment, which is what makes this Dockerfile in scope at all; the path carries no src/test.
row_derivations.file_anchors_at_the_pin: The 71-line k8s Dockerfile. Line 36 opens the RUN block this record names, and line 71, the last, is USER ${spark_uid}. Verified in the pinned clone at 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d.
row_derivations.shares_a_target_with: rejection 0, which is the other element of this same Misconfigurations array. One array, one row and one rejection -- which is what makes this the pair that proves the rejection is a record-level outcome rather than a section-level or target-level one.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Misconfigurations
row_derivations.message_note: This is the near-miss row, and the reason it exists. The record has no Title at all, so route 1 is defeated exactly as it is on both rejected records; its Description carries text, so route 2 succeeds and the record becomes a row. It is the difference between defeating one route and defeating them all, held as data rather than asserted in prose. Its Message -- "Add HEALTHCHECK instruction in your Dockerfile" -- is the remediation instruction and is not consulted, so the message is the Description and not the shorter, more headline-like Message.
row_derivations.start_line_absent_reason: This record's CauseMetadata carries Provider and Service only, and the record carries no top-level StartLine, so both entries of _SECTION_START_LINE_PATHS for this section come back empty. That absence is the real tool's own shape rather than an artefact of the derivation: the record in harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json this one descends from carries the same CauseMetadata with no StartLine, so Trivy really does report a Dockerfile misconfiguration with no line attached -- a missing HEALTHCHECK is a property of the whole file rather than of one line. Absence is never a rejection; only a start_line present and not a usable line number is, and that is a different fixture.
row_derivations.start_line_is_absent_not_zero: The field is null rather than 0. start_line_zero_read_as_absent stays 0 because no record here states a zero; that counter exists for a producer that writes 0 meaning "no line", and this record writes nothing at all.
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: a misconfiguration carries no CweIDs by the artifact's shape
row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: no VulnerabilityID on this section's records
row_derivations.in_scope_note: The same glob as row 0, matching through a deeper tail: ** matches docker/ before src/main and then dockerfiles/spark/bindings/R/Dockerfile after it. Two distinct files under one glob, which is why the expansion is arithmetic rather than a second scope.
row_derivations.file_anchors_at_the_pin: The R bindings Dockerfile, 47 lines, whose last three are the ARG spark_uid=185 and USER ${spark_uid} pair. A different file from row 0's and a different length, verified in the pinned clone.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Secrets, which SUPPORTED_SECTIONS maps to secret. See scanner_class_falsifiability: this is the record whose content would mislead a sniff.
row_derivations.message_note: The secret route is covered here by a valid record, and by the route the adapter prefers after the redacted Match: this record carries no Match member at all, so route 1 finds nothing and route 2 returns the rule Title "Asymmetric Private Key" -- the rule's name, carrying no character of any matched value. That is the deliberate choice recorded under secret_route_safety: the message-less record is kept out of Secrets[] precisely so that no fixture committed to git needs to carry secret-adjacent material to defeat a third route.
row_derivations.start_line_note: A secret states StartLine at the top level, not inside CauseMetadata. 446 is within the file's 2179 lines; the record's EndLine of 448 is not read.
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: no CweIDs on a secret record
row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: no VulnerabilityID on a secret record
row_derivations.package_coordinate_absence_is_not_a_reje: Secrets is outside _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS: a secret is a finding about a file, not about a package.
row_derivations.in_scope_note: A Python source file under the authoritative glob. The literal src/test exclusion does not reach python/pyspark/**, which is why Python modules there are in scope; this file is not a test module in any case.
row_derivations.file_anchors_at_the_pin: python/pyspark/sql/connect/client/core.py, 2179 lines, whose line 446 sits inside the channel-credentials block that builds grpc credentials. Verified in the pinned clone.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Vulnerabilities
row_derivations.message_note: The surviving sibling of rejection 1: the same section, the same enclosing element and the same two routes, with this record's Title carrying text. So the fixture holds both outcomes of one section's route tuple within one Results[] element.
row_derivations.severity_note: UNKNOWN is a mapped literal, not an unmapped one: severity.py's label table bands NEGLIGIBLE, INFO, INFORMATIONAL, UNKNOWN and NONE to Info. So the basis is label, severity_native keeps UNKNOWN, severity_norm is Info, and severity_basis_unmapped_literal stays 0. severity_norm is never absent, whatever the literal.
row_derivations.path_note: The record carries no PkgPath, so the Target stands unrefined. It is the same Target the rejected record at index 0 of this array carries, which is why a reader must not read the rejection as a statement about dev/package-lock.json: this row comes from the same file and is kept.
row_derivations.start_line_absent_reason: a vulnerability declares no line information
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: this record carries no CweIDs member
row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: NSWG-ECO-519 is a Node.js Security WG identifier and is not CVE-shaped, so it stays in rule_id and cve is absent rather than being reshaped
row_derivations.package_coordinate_level: 2 -- a package URL on the matching enclosing Packages[] entry
row_derivations.package_coordinate_note: This is the level a reader most easily skips, and getting it wrong is the difference between pkg:npm/handlebars@4.5.3 and npm:handlebars@4.5.3. The record itself carries no PkgIdentifier, so level 1 fails; the enclosing Results[3].Packages holds an entry whose ID is handlebars@4.5.3, matched to this record's PkgID by exact equality, and that entry's Identifier.PURL is pkg:npm/handlebars@4.5.3. Level 2 precedes the ecosystem coordinate of level 3, so the PURL wins and the ecosystem route is never reached.
row_derivations.package_coordinate_match_evidence: exact equality of /Results/3/Vulnerabilities/1/PkgID with /Results/3/Packages/1/ID -- no prefix match, no normalisation and no version-range reasoning
row_derivations.package_coordinate_is_required_here: Vulnerabilities is the one section in _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS, so a record from which no coordinate could be formed would be an unformable_package_coordinate rejection rather than a row with a null field. This record forms one at level 2, so it is a row. That condition's own fixture is reject-trivy-no-package-coordinate.json.
row_derivations.in_scope_note: dev/package-lock.json is outside the twelve globs; kept with in_scope false and counted under rows_out_of_scope. A dependency-oriented runner legitimately reaching a manifest outside the twelve roots is a kept row, never a filtered one.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Vulnerabilities
row_derivations.severity_note: The record carries a CVSS table with ghsa, nvd and redhat entries whose V3Scores are 3.7, 5.3 and 5.3 -- scores that would band Low, Medium and Medium. None is consulted: the label LOW is in the mapped vocabulary, so severity.py's label-over-score precedence takes it and the basis is label. The scores' presence is recorded under severity_cvss_entries_present, which counts what was available rather than what was used, and that separation is what makes the precedence checkable instead of merely asserted.
row_derivations.path_note: The Target is "Node.js", which names an ecosystem and not a file, and PkgPath names the manifest the package was found in. Only Vulnerabilities declares a per-record path field, so this is the fixture's one refinement. "Node.js" is not an archive container -- paths.ARCHIVE_EXTENSIONS covers .jar .war .ear .zip .tar .tgz .tar.gz .aar .nupkg .whl .egg and nothing like it -- so no <container>!<member> serialization arises and non_filesystem_paths stays 0.
row_derivations.start_line_absent_reason: a vulnerability declares no line information
row_derivations.cwe_note: The record names exactly one weakness, CWE-400, so the ascending-numeric rule selects it without a contest and multi_valued_cwe_records is not bumped by this row. The fixture's only multi-valued CweIDs array belongs to rejection 1 and is never read.
row_derivations.cve_note: CVE-2017-16137 is CVE-shaped, so it is both the rule_id and the cve. The VendorIDs entry GHSA-gxpj-cx7g-858c is not a CVE and is not read into the field.
row_derivations.package_coordinate_level: 1 -- a package URL on the record itself
row_derivations.package_coordinate_note: Level 1 resolves, so no enclosing Packages inventory is consulted -- and this Results[] element carries none, which is why the level ordering matters here rather than merely being stated.
row_derivations.in_scope_note: In scope on the strength of the refinement rather than of the Target: "Node.js" matches no glob, and core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json matches core/src/main/**. Reading the Target as the path would flip this row to in_scope false and lose the only in-scope dependency coordinate in the fixture.
row_derivations.file_anchors_at_the_pin: core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json, five lines and 80 bytes, carrying a name of spark-ui, a license of Apache License 2.0 and "type": "module", with no dependencies block and no lockfile beside it. It is the only manifest-shaped file inside the twelve globs, which is why a dependency coordinate can be in scope at all.

secret_route_safety.choice: Neither message-less record is placed in Secrets[]. Both sit where their defeat costs nothing: one in Misconfigurations[] and one in Vulnerabilities[].
secret_route_safety.why: A secret has three message routes and the first is the redacted Match. Defeating all three would mean authoring a secret record whose Match is absent or emptied while the record still reads as a plausible secret finding -- and the pressure that creates is to add secret-adjacent material to a fixture that is committed to git. This tree is collected normally: the root .gitignore's only relevant line matches artifacts/, so nothing here is excluded. The safe construction is to defeat a two-route section instead, which is exactly as strong a test of _message: the function is section-generic and walks whatever tuple its section names.
secret_route_safety.what_is_given_up_and_what_is_not: What is given up is a missing_message rejection whose section is Secrets. What is not given up is any coverage of the secret route itself: row 2 exercises it with a valid record, taking route 2 because that record carries no Match, so the Match-first ordering and the Title fallback are both asserted on real data.
secret_route_safety.do_not_fix_this_later: A future reader may notice no secret is rejected here and move a defective record into Secrets[] to "complete the matrix". That would trade a structural guarantee for symmetry the requirement does not ask for. If a Secrets-section missing_message case is ever wanted, the way to get it is a record with no Match, no Title and no Description -- three absent members and no material added -- and it belongs in its own fixture with its own expected file, not by editing this one.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and the result_index / section / record_index triple name the same record. The triple is carried as well because normalize.adapters.trivy builds its rejection identity from exactly result_index, section, record_index and Target, adding rule_id once the rule step passes, so a produced Rejection's record_identity and this expectation can be compared directly without translating one coordinate system into the other.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_MISSING_MESSAGE constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten. Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, so the class name is what carries the assertion.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, section, rule identifier, message, path, start_line, package coordinate. Steps 1 to 3 all pass: it is a JSON object, Misconfigurations is a supported section so the class is established, and its ID of DS-0031 is a valid rule identifier. That is deliberate, so the only thing left to reject it for is its message.

text_present_but_not_consulted.Message: Possible exposure of secret env "SPARK_HOME" in ENV
text_present_but_not_consulted.Resolution: Use secret mount if secrets are needed during image build. Use volume mount if secret files are needed during container runtime.
text_present_but_not_consulted.why: Message is the located instance and Resolution is the remediation instruction; _SECTION_MESSAGE_FIELDS names neither for this section. This record is the one that holds that decision to account: it has real text in the document and is still rejected, so adding Message to the misconfiguration route tuple would turn this expectation red rather than passing unnoticed. The Message quoted here is the fixture's own words, and the environment variable it names carries a path, not a credential.

rejections.expected_detail: the Misconfigurations record carries no message: none of Title, Description holds text
rejections.expected_detail_note: The detail is the sub-reason AAP 0.5.4 requires a rejection to carry, and it is quoted because a class name alone would not distinguish this record from the other rejection below -- both are missing_message and only the section and the identity differ. A test may assert the class exactly and the detail by its distinguishing substrings rather than by full-string equality; the section name in the detail is the distinguishing part.
rejections.record_identity_note: Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and never the record itself. The Target is carried because a rejection with no location is a rejection nobody can look up.

never_reached.path_resolution: step 5 -- the record's Target resolves perfectly well and is the same Target row 0 uses, so no path condition is in play
never_reached.start_line: step 6 -- the record's CauseMetadata.StartLine of 62 is never examined, so non_integer_start_line is not in play and this record contributes nothing to start_line_absent
never_reached.package_coordinate: step 7 -- and it would have been absent legitimately in any case, since Misconfigurations is outside _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS
never_reached.severity: the label CRITICAL is never mapped, so no Critical band is produced and severity_basis_label counts this record not at all
never_reached.counters: path_kind_*, rows_class_*, rows_in_scope, rows_out_of_scope and every package_coordinate_* counter are bumped only once nothing can reject, so this record appears in none of them. It appears in records_misconfigurations, which is bumped by the array's length before the walk.

rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no message to put in the row. message is one of emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS, and the alternatives -- dropping the record, or filling the field from the Message, the Resolution or the rule identifier -- would each either hide the record or attribute words to the tool that the tool did not write as its message. Counting it under a named class keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: The rejected record is never fed to the severity tally, so its CRITICAL never reaches severity-map.md. That document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains, and this record contributes none -- which is why no row below carries severity_norm Critical even though the fixture contains a CRITICAL literal.

rejections.locator_note: As above: the pointer and the triple name the same record, and the triple is the shape the adapter's own identity takes.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_MISSING_MESSAGE constant -- the same literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES. Two records, one class, and rejections_by_class carries the count of 2 rather than two separate entries.
rejections.classification_step: step 4, exactly as above. Steps 1 to 3 pass: it is a JSON object, Vulnerabilities is a supported section, and CVE-2021-3749 is a valid rule identifier.
rejections.the_two_variants_of_one_class: This record is the present-but-empty variant and rejection 0 is the absent-member variant. _message treats them identically, through _non_empty_string, and the fixture carries both so that a change making an empty string pass -- a truthiness test replaced by a key-presence test, say -- is caught here rather than in production. A producer really does emit an empty Title: the member is a plain string in report.go, not an optional.
rejections.expected_detail: the Vulnerabilities record carries no message: none of Title, Description holds text
rejections.expected_detail_note: Identical to rejection 0's except for the section name, which is the substring that distinguishes the two.
rejections.record_identity_note: The Target is out of scope, which is beside the point: in_scope is a property of a row and this record produces none. A rejection is not counted in rows_out_of_scope.

never_reached.path_resolution: step 5 -- the Target resolves, and row 3 comes from the same one
never_reached.start_line: step 6 -- a vulnerability declares no line information in any case, so this record contributes nothing to start_line_absent
never_reached.package_coordinate: step 7 -- and this is the interesting one: the record carries PkgIdentifier.PURL pkg:npm/axios@0.21.0, so a coordinate was formable at level 1 and is still never formed. A well-formed dependency record is rejected for its message alone, which is what makes the rejection attributable.
never_reached.cwe_selection: the record's CweIDs array holds CWE-1333 and CWE-400 -- two identifiers in producer order that disagrees with the ascending-numeric rule -- and no selection is ever made on it. That is why multi_valued_cwe_records is 0 in a fixture that plainly contains a multi-valued CweIDs array, and it is the single most likely value for a reviewer to "correct".
never_reached.cve_selection: CVE-2021-3749 is CVE-shaped and would have become the cve field; it stays in the identity above and reaches no row
never_reached.severity: the label HIGH and the three CVSS entries -- ghsa 7.5, nvd 7.8 and 7.5, redhat 7.5 -- are all left unread, so severity_cvss_entries_present counts 1 rather than 2

rejections.why_not_a_row: As above: no message, and message is never absent from a row. Filling it from the VulnerabilityID would put the string CVE-2021-3749 in the message column of a dataset whose consumers read that column as tool prose, and filling it from PkgName would put a package name there. Both are inference, and AAP 0.5.4's rule is to reject rather than infer.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: Its HIGH never reaches severity-map.md through this record. Two surviving rows do carry HIGH, from other records, which is exactly why the tally must be fed per emitted row rather than per record walked.

prohibitions_observed.no_secret_value_in_any_field: No field on any row carries material from a matched secret. Row 2's message is the rule's Title, "Asymmetric Private Key", which names the kind of key and contains no key; that record carries no Match member, no Code excerpt and no redaction, and the adapter reads no secret member beyond Match, Title and Description in any case. The string "Match" does not appear in the fixture at all. That is a structural guarantee rather than an incidental one, which matters because this tree is committed to git: the root .gitignore's only relevant line matches artifacts/, so nothing here is excluded from collection.
prohibitions_observed.no_cross_tool_interpretation: Rows 3 and 4 are vulnerability findings and dependency-check's expected rows also carry vulnerability findings. Nothing here compares the two, ranks them, explains why one tool reported something another did not, or comments on a location both reached. Nothing here says what Trivy's two message-less records demonstrate about Trivy, either: the rejections are facts about this fixture and this adapter, not a characterisation of the tool.
prohibitions_observed.no_judging_and_no_deduplication: No row is marked real, important, a false positive or a duplicate, and no rejected record is called a tool defect. Rows 0 and 1 name the same rule family on two files and are two rows; rows 3 and 4 name different packages in different manifests and are two rows. Nothing is collapsed and nothing is ranked. The two rejections share a class and are two rejections, counted as 2 under one class name rather than merged into one finding about the fixture.
prohibitions_observed.no_inference: Every value above names the member it came from. Where a value could not be formed the field is null with the reason recorded, and where a record's message could not be obtained it is a counted rejection rather than a guessed string. The one place inference would be easiest -- filling a missing message from a neighbouring text member -- is the exact thing this fixture exists to forbid.

discrepancies_recorded.subject: how many records this fixture rejects
discrepancies_recorded.expectation_as_written: this file's own brief describes one record from which no message can be obtained, and states a rejection count of 1
discrepancies_recorded.what_the_inputs_actually_hold: Two records have every message route their section offers defeated, and both are missing_message. /Results/3/Vulnerabilities/0 is the one the brief describes exactly -- Title and Description present and non-empty in neither. /Results/0/Misconfigurations/0 is the second: it carries no Title and no Description, and its only text is a Message, which _SECTION_MESSAGE_FIELDS deliberately does not name as a route for a misconfiguration. That record is the positive fixture's own DS-0031 with Title and Description removed, and expected/derived-trivy-features.rows.json's row_derivations[0] is where the "Message is deliberately not consulted" decision is written down -- so this record is that decision's falsification test, deliberately constructed and not an oversight.
discrepancies_recorded.resolution: Two rejections are asserted, under the one class, with rejections_by_class carrying missing_message 2 and rejection_classes_present carrying 1. The fixture is not edited. It is the input and this file is the assertion, and the dependency runs one way: editing the fixture to make the count match the brief would delete the only coverage anywhere in this tree of the Message-is-not-a-route decision, and would overwrite an input to satisfy a summary of it. The brief authorises a fixture correction in exactly one circumstance -- the defective record sitting in Secrets[] -- and that circumstance does not hold, since the two records sit in Misconfigurations[] and Vulnerabilities[]. No other file records this fixture's digest, so nothing downstream depends on the count being 1. Everything else the brief asks for is unaffected: one class, named verbatim from paths.REJECT_MISSING_MESSAGE; per-class counts stated; parse status partial; the multi-route problem recorded; and the arithmetic still closing, as 7 == 5 + 2.

discrepancies_recorded.subject: whether every surviving misconfiguration row carries a start_line
discrepancies_recorded.expectation_as_written: start_line null on every vulnerability row, present on secrets and misconfigurations
discrepancies_recorded.what_the_inputs_actually_hold: True of the section shapes and true of three of the five rows, but not of row 1. Its record's CauseMetadata carries Provider and Service only and it has no top-level StartLine, so both entries of _SECTION_START_LINE_PATHS come back empty and start_line is null. This is not an artefact of the fixture's derivation: the record it descends from in harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json carries the same CauseMetadata with no StartLine, so the real tool emits this misconfiguration with no line attached. Both vulnerability rows are null as expected, and the secret row and the other misconfiguration row carry 446 and 36.
discrepancies_recorded.resolution: Row 1's start_line is asserted null, and start_line_absent is 3 rather than 2. Absence is never a rejection -- only a start_line present and not a usable line number is, which is a different fixture -- so this is a legitimate row with a legitimately absent optional field. The invariant that does hold without exception is the one worth testing: no vulnerability row carries a start_line.

discrepancies_recorded.subject: how many k8s Dockerfiles the fixture covers
discrepancies_recorded.expectation_as_written: the k8s Dockerfile, 71 lines, in the singular
discrepancies_recorded.what_the_inputs_actually_hold: Two distinct Dockerfile Targets, both in scope under the same glob: resource-managers/kubernetes/docker/src/main/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile at 71 lines, which is row 0 and the one the brief names, and .../spark/bindings/R/Dockerfile at 47 lines, which is row 1. Both line counts were verified in the pinned clone at 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d.
discrepancies_recorded.resolution: Both rows are listed in full with their own file line counts, and the second is named rather than folded into the first. The second Target is not incidental: it is what carries the near-miss record whose Description survives, so the fixture needs a second file to hold the boundary the first file's records do not.

how_to_check_this_file: It parses as JSON, and every row carries exactly the twelve keys of emit.FIELDS in that order -- compared against the imported constant rather than a copy of it.

Both rejections' reject_class is a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, asserted with `in` against the imported tuple, and equal to paths.REJECT_MISSING_MESSAGE. rejections_by_class sums to counts.rejections.

Re-walk the fixture and assert each row's scanner_class equals the class its enclosing array dictates, and each rejection's section equals the array it was read from. Row 2 is the one that fails if the derivation is ever inverted.

Neither defective record is in Secrets[]: re-read the fixture and confirm /Results/0/Misconfigurations/0 and /Results/3/Vulnerabilities/0 are the two, and that /Results/2/Secrets/0 has a non-empty Title. If a defective record is ever found in Secrets[], the fixture must be corrected rather than this file.

No surviving row's message equals or contains either rejected record's rule identifier, package name or path, and no rejected record's identifier contains a row's message -- substring comparison in both directions over DS-0031, CVE-2021-3749, axios, resource-managers/kubernetes/docker/src/main/dockerfiles/spark/Dockerfile and dev/package-lock.json. This is what "no message is synthesised" means as a check rather than a claim.

Every row derived from Vulnerabilities[] has start_line null; the secret row's start_line and the row 0 misconfiguration's are integers within their files' real line counts, 2179 and 71; and row 1's is null with no StartLine anywhere in its record.

The valid secret row's message is exactly its record's Title, and its record carries no Match member. Grep this file and the fixture for any Match or Secret value: the only occurrence of "Secret" in the fixture is the section key, "Match" does not occur in it at all, and no asterisk redaction appears in any row here.
Licenses and ExperimentalModifiedFindings are present and empty on all five Results[] elements, so trivy.validate_finding_sections returns None and no halt pre-empts the rejections.

The out-of-scope row is present rather than dropped and its in_scope is false; every severity_norm is one of Critical, High, Medium, Low, Info; no path is absolute or empty; row 4's path is the PkgPath refinement and not its Target.

The five rows, two rejections and seven raw records satisfy raw_finding_records == rows + rejections against reconcile.count_records("trivy", doc)'s independent traversal, and records_vulnerabilities + records_secrets + records_misconfigurations equals the same 7.
